keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 557-559: Cliopatria's Chen row begins in 561 but the infobox has 'Established: 16 November 557'. Wang Lin, 'who controlled modern Hunan and eastern Hubei', refused Chen's summons in 557, attacked in winter 559 and was beaten in spring 560, so the 561 shape is cut by those two provinces for 557-559. The infobox gives no area (only 'Administrative divisions in 572').

Shape unchanged, valid 560-572 (the Chen took Hunan from Wang Lin in spring 560 and the Western Liang's half of Xiao Zhuang's territory in spring 561). 1.01 M km2; no infobox area to compare. The 573 and 580 keyframes carry the Yangtze-Huai strip.

ledger.note: 557: Chen Baxian founds the Chen at Jiankang. 'Established: 16 November 557'; he 'took the initiative to establish a new empire in Southern China'. The land is the Cliopatria 561 shape minus Wang Lin's provinces, the researcher's reading.

region.text: Wang Lin's holdings: 'modern Hunan and eastern Hubei'

ledger.note: 559: Wang Lin attacks the Chen. 'Wang Lin launched a major attack on Chen in winter 559' from the Hunan and eastern Hubei he 'controlled'; he had declared Xiao Zhuang emperor at Ying Province after the Northern Qi returned Xiao Zhuang.

region.text: Wang Lin's holdings: 'modern Hunan and eastern Hubei'

ledger.note: 560: Hou Tian defeats Wang Lin. 'He was initially successful, but by spring 560, Hou Tian defeated Wang,' and Wang and Xiao Zhuang fled to the Northern Qi.

region.text: Wang Lin's Hunan, half of Xiao Zhuang's former territory

ledger.note: 560: the Chen take Hunan and half of Xiao Zhuang's land. 'Chen forces took about half of Xiao Zhuang's territory, while the other half went to the Northern Zhou-supported Western Liang.' The page does not say which half; Hunan is the researcher's reading.

region.text: Ying Province, modern eastern Hubei, the other half of Xiao Zhuang's territory

ledger.note: 561: the Western Liang cedes the other half. 'Hou Tian negotiated with the Northern Zhou for the Western Liang to cede this territory to the Chen in spring 561'; Xiao Zhuang's capital was Ying Province, modern eastern Hubei. [Reviewer ea-03-f, 2026-10-19: confidence lowered from 3 to 2: the Chen page does not say where the ceded half of Xiao Zhuang's territory lay; the Wuhan radius is the researcher's reading]

570: the Guang Province rising ends. 'He was beheaded in 570.'

ledger.note: 573: the Chen take the land between the Yangtze and the Huai. Wu Mingche's campaign 'gained most of the territory between the Yangtze River and the Huai River'; 'By fall 573, Wu put the important city Shouyang (Anhui) under siege' and took it, killing the Qi commander Wang Lin.

ledger.note: 577: the Chen attack Pengcheng. 'In winter 577, Wu put Pengcheng (Xuzhou, Jiangsu) under siege'; Wang Gui of the Northern Zhou crushed him in spring 578; the Zhou attacked the Chen in winter 579.

ledger.note: 587: two Western Liang officials surrender to the Chen. 'In fall 587, while Emperor Jing of Western Liang was at the Sui capital,' Xiao Yan and Xiao Huan surrendered, fearing a Sui attack on Jiangling; Chen made them provincial governors. The page does not name their provinces; Cliopatria's 587 shape adds only about 390 km2. The Sui took the rest of the Western Liang the same year.

ledger.note: 589: Jiankang falls. 'Spring 589: Heruo Bi crossed from Guangling, and Han Qinhu crossed at Caishi, sandwiching Jiankang'; Chen Shubao was found hiding in a well and captured.

Infobox 'Disestablished 10 February 589' (the text places the collapse in spring 589); 'By 589, Sui troops entered Jiankang and the last emperor of Chen surrendered' (Sui page); the Sui infobox gives 3,000,000 km2 for the united empire in 589.

notes:
CLIOPATRIA ROW. The row (561-591) starts four years after the state (16 November 557) and ends two years after it (10 February 589); the 587 shape adds only 390 km2 to the 561 shape. The 561 shape is unchanged from 561 to 586 although the Chen held the Yangtze-Huai strip from 573 to the winter of 579-580 (new keyframes chen-dynasty_573 and _580); the strip is approximated by Cliopatria's Northern Qi 561 increment.
COUNTERPARTS NEEDING A DOSSIER. Wang Lin's regime (Xiao Zhuang's Liang), 557-560, held 'modern Hunan and eastern Hubei' and was backed by the Northern Qi: a rebel-type state with no Cliopatria row (suggested slug wang-lin-s-liang); the Chen ledger names it by text. Ouyang He's Guang Province rising (569-570) is a one-year revolt, not a state. Xiao Bo's 557 rising from Guang Province ended by his own generals and is not mapped.
AREA. The Chen infobox gives no area; the 1.01 M km2 shape could not be compared.
NOT ON THE PAGES OPENED. The Chen page does not use the words Lingnan, Lady Xian or Hengyang, does not name the Chen provinces or say how far Chen power reached into Jiaozhou ('Giao Chau Province (Chen northern Vietnam)' appears only as the region of the 541 Ly Bon rising; Cliopatria's Chen shape reaches Vietnam in only two cells). The Western Liang page opened is silent on the Chen. 
PAGE BUDGET. Chen dynasty, plus the shared Emperor Wu of Northern Zhou, Sui dynasty and Western Liang pages. A gap-filler could open 'Chen Baxian', 'Emperor Xuan of Chen' and the Hou Jing and Xiao Zhuang pages for the founding years.
